# HarborBuddy

> HarborBuddy is a self-hosted Docker container updater and Watchtower alternative. It runs as one container on a Docker host, pulls each running container's image reference on a schedule, replaces a container only when the pulled image ID differs from the running one, waits for the replacement's health check, and automatically restores the original container when the update fails.

Full text of every page, for language models: https://mikeo7.github.io/HarborBuddy/llms-full.txt

## Key facts

- Latest release: v0.1.0 (2026-11-06). Image: `ghcr.io/mikeo7/harborbuddy:0.1` for linux/amd64, linux/arm64, and linux/arm/v7.
- Written in Go; ships as a single static binary in a container image.
- Targets one standalone Docker Engine per HarborBuddy instance. Its integration tests also run against Podman's Docker-compatible API. It does not support Docker Swarm tasks or Kubernetes.
- Detects updates by comparing image IDs after pulling the container's existing tag, not by tag names. It does not move containers to newer version tags.
- Update sequence: rename the original to a backup, stop it, create and start the replacement, wait for `healthy` (or two seconds of process stability without a health check), then remove the backup. A failed create, start, or health check restores the original.
- Updates cause a brief interruption; HarborBuddy is not a zero-downtime updater. Rollback is best-effort.
- Recovers updates interrupted by a crash: stopped backups from the last 48 hours are renamed back and restarted on the next cycle.
- Container selection: all running containers by default; opt out with the label `com.harborbuddy.autoupdate=false`; allow and deny image patterns, where deny wins.
- Schedules: an interval (default 12h) or one daily `HH:MM` time in an IANA timezone.
- Dry-run mode (`HARBORBUDDY_DRY_RUN=true` or `--dry-run`) pulls images and reports decisions without changing containers.
- Self-update through a short-lived helper container; a failed self-update image is not retried for 24 hours.
- Cleanup: dangling images older than 24 hours by default; stopped containers, unused tagged images, networks, volumes, and build cache are opt-in.
- Not supported yet: notifications, a web UI or HTTP API, and authenticated private registries.
- Requires read/write Docker socket access, which is equivalent to root on the host.
- License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (source-available, not open source). Free for personal and other noncommercial use; commercial use is not permitted.
- Maintainer: MikeO7 (https://github.com/MikeO7). Source: https://github.com/MikeO7/HarborBuddy

- [Documentation home](https://mikeo7.github.io/HarborBuddy/docs/): index of all guides
- [Quick start](https://mikeo7.github.io/HarborBuddy/docs/quick-start/): Docker Compose setup, dry run, and enabling updates
- [How updates work](https://mikeo7.github.io/HarborBuddy/docs/how-updates-work/): detection, the seven-step replacement, rollback, and crash recovery
- [Choose which containers update](https://mikeo7.github.io/HarborBuddy/docs/choosing-containers/): opt-out label and allow and deny patterns
- [Configuration reference](https://mikeo7.github.io/HarborBuddy/docs/configuration/): every environment variable, YAML key, and CLI flag
- [Self-update](https://mikeo7.github.io/HarborBuddy/docs/self-update/): helper-based self-update and failure handling
- [Cleanup](https://mikeo7.github.io/HarborBuddy/docs/cleanup/): image and resource cleanup and keep rules
- [Limits and requirements](https://mikeo7.github.io/HarborBuddy/docs/limitations/): unsupported containers, security, and licensing
